sanskrit: ā sa̱tyo yā̍tu ma̱ghavā̍m̐ ṛjī̱ṣī drava̍ntv asya̱ hara̍ya̱ upa̍ naḥ | tasmā̱ id andha̍ḥ suṣumā su̱dakṣa̍m i̱hābhi̍pi̱tvaṁ ka̍rate gṛṇā̱naḥ ||
english: Let the true, bountiful Maghavan come hither; let his tawny steeds run toward us. For him we have pressed the soma to gladden him — the wise and able one who, hearing our praise, fashions the meeting here.

sanskrit: ava̍ sya śū̱rādhva̍no̱ nānte̱ 'smin no̍ a̱dya sava̍ne ma̱ndadhyai̍ | śaṁsā̍ty u̱ktham u̱śane̍va ve̱dhāś ci̍ki̱tuṣe̍ asu̱ryā̍ya̱ manma̍ ||
english: Let the hero of good courses come down to take delight at this our pressing today. The wise one recites the laud like Uśanas the sage — a prayer for the discerning, sovereign lord.

sanskrit: ka̱vir na ni̱ṇyaṁ vi̱dathā̍ni̱ sādha̱n vṛṣā̱ yat seka̍ṁ vipipā̱no arcā̍t | di̱va i̱tthā jī̍janat sa̱pta kā̱rūn ahnā̍ cic cakrur va̱yunā̍ gṛ̱ṇanta̍ḥ ||
english: Like a sage accomplishing deep deliberations, the bull, drinking deeply, sang the libation. He thus begot the seven bards of heaven — they who, praising, fashioned understanding even by day.

sanskrit: sva1̱̍r yad vedi̍ su̱dṛśī̍kam a̱rkair mahi̱ jyotī̍ rurucu̱r yad dha̱ vasto̍ḥ | a̱ndhā tamā̍ṁsi̱ dudhi̍tā vi̱cakṣe̱ nṛbhya̍ś cakāra̱ nṛta̍mo a̱bhiṣṭau̍ ||
english: When the altar shone beautiful with hymns as the great light blazed at the house, he shook off the blinding darknesses so as to see — the most manly one at the invocation wrought this for men.

sanskrit: va̱va̱kṣa indro̱ ami̍tam ṛjī̱ṣy u1̱̍bhe ā pa̍prau̱ roda̍sī mahi̱tvā | ata̍ś cid asya mahi̱mā vi re̍cy a̱bhi yo viśvā̱ bhuva̍nā ba̱bhūva̍ ||
english: Indra has swelled immeasurably — the mighty soma-drinker; with his greatness he filled both world-halves. Even beyond this his greatness streams forth — he who has pervaded all existing beings.

sanskrit: viśvā̍ni śa̱kro naryā̍ṇi vi̱dvān a̱po ri̍reca̱ sakhi̍bhi̱r nikā̍maiḥ | aśmā̍naṁ ci̱d ye bi̍bhi̱dur vaco̍bhir vra̱jaṁ goma̍ntam u̱śijo̱ vi va̍vruḥ ||
english: The mighty Śakra, knowing all manly deeds, poured forth the waters with his willing comrades. Those Uśijas who with their words caused even the stone to tremble — they burst open the cattle-pen.

sanskrit: a̱po vṛ̱traṁ va̍vri̱vāṁsa̱m parā̍ha̱n prāva̍t te̱ vajra̍m pṛthi̱vī sace̍tāḥ | prārṇā̍ṁsi samu̱driyā̍ṇy aino̱ḥ pati̱r bhava̱ñ chava̍sā śūra dhṛṣṇo ||
english: He struck down Vṛtra who had covered the waters; the earth, understanding, favored your bolt. You set the ocean-bound floods free — be their lord, O hero, bold and mighty.

sanskrit: a̱po yad adri̍m puruhūta̱ darda̍r ā̱vir bhu̍vat sa̱ramā̍ pū̱rvyaṁ te̍ | sa no̍ ne̱tā vāja̱m ā da̍rṣi̱ bhūri̍ṁ go̱trā ru̱jann aṅgi̍robhir gṛṇā̱naḥ ||
english: When, O Puruhūta, you burst the rock asunder for the waters, Saramā went before you. May he lead us and strike open ample booty — praised with hymns, breaking the cowpens with the Aṅgirasas.

sanskrit: acchā̍ ka̱viṁ nṛ̍maṇo gā a̱bhiṣṭau̱ sva̍rṣātā maghava̱n nādha̍mānam | ū̱tibhi̱s tam i̍ṣaṇo dyu̱mnahū̍tau̱ ni mā̱yāvā̱n abra̍hmā̱ dasyu̍r arta ||
english: Drive the cows, O Maghavan of manly counsel, toward the wise poet at the invocation — the winner of heaven's light who entreats you. With your aids urge him on as they call for glory; the wily, prayer-less Dasyu shall be cast down.

sanskrit: ā da̍syu̱ghnā mana̍sā yā̱hy asta̱m bhuva̍t te̱ kutsa̍ḥ sa̱khye nikā̍maḥ | sve yonau̱ ni ṣa̍data̱ṁ sarū̍pā̱ vi vā̍ṁ cikitsad ṛta̱cid dha̱ nārī̍ ||
english: Come home with a Dasyu-slaying mind; may Kutsa be willing in your friendship. Let the two of you, like-formed, sit in your own birthplace — the woman who truly knows ṛta perceived you both.

sanskrit: yāsi̱ kutse̍na sa̱ratha̍m ava̱syus to̱do vāta̍sya̱ haryo̱r īśā̍naḥ | ṛ̱jrā vāja̱ṁ na gadhya̱ṁ yuyū̍ṣan ka̱vir yad aha̱n pāryā̍ya̱ bhūṣā̍t ||
english: You go in one chariot with Kutsa seeking aid — the goad, the master of Wind's two tawny steeds. Stretching straight as if trying for a prize of valor, the wise one shone when he smote for the crossing.

sanskrit: kutsā̍ya̱ śuṣṇa̍m a̱śuṣa̱ṁ ni ba̍rhīḥ prapi̱tve ahna̱ḥ kuya̍vaṁ sa̱hasrā̍ | sa̱dyo dasyū̱n pra mṛ̍ṇa ku̱tsyena̱ pra sūra̍ś ca̱kraṁ vṛ̍hatād a̱bhīke̍ ||
english: For Kutsa you laid low Śuṣṇa the drought-demon, the one of bad grain and his thousands at the afternoon watch. Crush the Dasyus at once with Kutsa's weapons; let the sun's wheel roll forth in the battle.

sanskrit: tvam pipru̱m mṛga̍yaṁ śūśu̱vāṁsa̍m ṛ̱jiśva̍ne vaidathi̱nāya̍ randhīḥ | pa̱ñcā̱śat kṛ̱ṣṇā ni va̍paḥ sa̱hasrātka̱ṁ na puro̍ jari̱mā vi da̍rdaḥ ||
english: You subdued Pipru and Mṛgaya the swelling demon for Ṛjiśvan Vaidathina. You mowed down fifty black demons; like an aged man's stronghold, you burst it asunder by the thousands.

sanskrit: sūra̍ upā̱ke ta̱nva1̱̍ṁ dadhā̍no̱ vi yat te̱ cety a̱mṛta̍sya̱ varpa̍ḥ | mṛ̱go na ha̱stī tavi̍ṣīm uṣā̱ṇaḥ si̱ṁho na bhī̱ma āyu̍dhāni̱ bibhra̍t ||
english: Placing his body near the sun, when the immortal's form shines forth in you — like a raging wild elephant in strength, like a terrible lion bearing his weapons.

sanskrit: indra̱ṁ kāmā̍ vasū̱yanto̍ agma̱n sva̍rmīḻhe̱ na sava̍ne cakā̱nāḥ | śra̱va̱syava̍ḥ śaśamā̱nāsa̍ u̱kthair oko̱ na ra̱ṇvā su̱dṛśī̍va pu̱ṣṭiḥ ||
english: Desiring goods and longing for Indra, they came to the pressing as to a contest for heaven. Striving for glory and striving with their hymns, they made it pleasant as a home, lovely as fine nourishment.

sanskrit: tam id va̱ indra̍ṁ su̱hava̍ṁ huvema̱ yas tā ca̱kāra̱ naryā̍ pu̱rūṇi̍ | yo māva̍te jari̱tre gadhya̍ṁ cin ma̱kṣū vāja̱m bhara̍ti spā̱rharā̍dhāḥ ||
english: Him indeed we call — Indra who is easy to invoke, he who performed those many manly deeds; who for the praising supplicant swiftly brings even abundant reward — he of enviable bounty.

sanskrit: ti̱gmā yad a̱ntar a̱śani̱ḥ patā̍ti̱ kasmi̍ñ cic chūra muhu̱ke janā̍nām | gho̱rā yad a̍rya̱ samṛ̍ti̱r bhavā̱ty adha̍ smā nas ta̱nvo̍ bodhi go̱pāḥ ||
english: When the sharp thunderbolt flies in the midst of peoples at some sudden moment, O hero — when the terrible encounter befalls, O lord, then be the guardian of our bodies.

sanskrit: bhuvo̍ 'vi̱tā vā̱made̍vasya dhī̱nām bhuva̱ḥ sakhā̍vṛ̱ko vāja̍sātau | tvām anu̱ prama̍ti̱m ā ja̍ganmoru̱śaṁso̍ jari̱tre vi̱śvadha̍ syāḥ ||
english: Be the protector of the thoughts of Vāmadeva; be a wolf-swift comrade in the winning of prizes. We have come following you for wisdom — may you always be of far-spread praise to the one who lauds you.

sanskrit: e̱bhir nṛbhi̍r indra tvā̱yubhi̍ṣ ṭvā ma̱ghava̍dbhir maghava̱n viśva̍ ā̱jau | dyāvo̱ na dyu̱mnair a̱bhi santo̍ a̱ryaḥ kṣa̱po ma̍dema śa̱rada̍ś ca pū̱rvīḥ ||
english: With these men, O Indra, these devotees of yours, these bountiful ones, O Maghavan, in every contest — like bright days abounding in glory, with noble men may we rejoice through nights and many autumns.

sanskrit: e̱ved indrā̍ya vṛṣa̱bhāya̱ vṛṣṇe̱ brahmā̍karma̱ bhṛga̍vo̱ na ratha̍m | nū ci̱d yathā̍ naḥ sa̱khyā vi̱yoṣa̱d asa̍n na u̱gro̍ 'vi̱tā ta̍nū̱pāḥ ||
english: Thus have we fashioned prayer-work for Indra the bull, the virile one, as the Bhṛgus fashion a chariot. May he not now separate from our friendship; may the fierce protector be our guardian of bodies.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: tvam ma̱hām̐ i̍ndra̱ tubhya̍ṁ ha̱ kṣā anu̍ kṣa̱tram ma̱ṁhanā̍ manyata̱ dyauḥ | tvaṁ vṛ̱traṁ śava̍sā jagha̱nvān sṛ̱jaḥ sindhū̱m̐r ahi̍nā jagrasā̱nān ||
english: You are great, O Indra — the earth followed your dominion in homage, heaven thought of you with generosity. You, having slain Vṛtra by your might, released the rivers that the serpent had swallowed.

sanskrit: tava̍ tvi̱ṣo jani̍man rejata̱ dyau reja̱d bhūmi̍r bhi̱yasā̱ svasya̍ ma̱nyoḥ | ṛ̱ghā̱yanta̍ su̱bhva1̱̍ḥ parva̍tāsa̱ ārda̱n dhanvā̍ni sa̱raya̍nta̱ āpa̍ḥ ||
english: At your birth the heaven trembled at the flash of your wrath, the earth trembled in fear of your very own fury. The mountains quaked in roaring, the fine-formed one; the deserts moistened as the waters flowed.

sanskrit: bhi̱nad gi̱riṁ śava̍sā̱ vajra̍m i̱ṣṇann ā̍viṣkṛṇvā̱naḥ sa̍hasā̱na oja̍ḥ | vadhī̍d vṛ̱traṁ vajre̍ṇa mandasā̱naḥ sara̱nn āpo̱ java̍sā ha̱tavṛ̍ṣṇīḥ ||
english: He split the mountain with his power, hurling his bolt, displaying his overwhelming might. He slew Vṛtra with his bolt in exhilaration; the waters flowed swiftly, their obstacle slain.

sanskrit: su̱vīra̍s te jani̱tā ma̍nyata̱ dyaur indra̍sya ka̱rtā svapa̍stamo bhūt | ya ī̍ṁ ja̱jāna̍ sva̱rya̍ṁ su̱vajra̱m ana̍pacyuta̱ṁ sada̍so̱ na bhūma̍ ||
english: Of good heroes, your father Heaven thought — the creator of Indra became the best craftsman. He who begot him as winner of heaven, well-armed with the bolt, unshakable as the ground of a seat.

sanskrit: ya eka̍ ic cyā̱vaya̍ti̱ pra bhūmā̱ rājā̍ kṛṣṭī̱nām pu̍ruhū̱ta indra̍ḥ | sa̱tyam e̍na̱m anu̱ viśve̍ madanti rā̱tiṁ de̱vasya̍ gṛṇa̱to ma̱ghona̍ḥ ||
english: He alone shakes the earth to its foundations — the king of peoples, the much-invoked Indra. All truly rejoice in him, in the gift of the bountiful god who is praised.

sanskrit: sa̱trā somā̍ abhavann asya̱ viśve̍ sa̱trā madā̍so bṛha̱to madi̍ṣṭhāḥ | sa̱trābha̍vo̱ vasu̍pati̱r vasū̍nā̱ṁ datre̱ viśvā̍ adhithā indra kṛ̱ṣṭīḥ ||
english: All the soma-drinks became his together, all the intoxications of the great one, most gladdening together. He became together the lord of all goods; at the giving, O Indra, you placed all peoples.

sanskrit: tvam adha̍ pratha̱maṁ jāya̍mā̱no 'me̱ viśvā̍ adhithā indra kṛ̱ṣṭīḥ | tvam prati̍ pra̱vata̍ ā̱śayā̍na̱m ahi̱ṁ vajre̍ṇa maghava̱n vi vṛ̍ścaḥ ||
english: You, when first being born, at once, O Indra, took up all peoples. You cut apart with the bolt, O Maghavan, the serpent lying on the downward slope.

sanskrit: sa̱trā̱haṇa̱ṁ dādhṛ̍ṣi̱ṁ tumra̱m indra̍m ma̱hām a̍pā̱raṁ vṛ̍ṣa̱bhaṁ su̱vajra̍m | hantā̱ yo vṛ̱traṁ sani̍to̱ta vāja̱ṁ dātā̍ ma̱ghāni̍ ma̱ghavā̍ su̱rādhā̍ḥ ||
english: The all-conquering, bold, strong, great, boundless Indra — the bull, well-armed with the bolt — the slayer of Vṛtra, the winner of prizes, the giver of gifts, the bountiful one of excellent bounty.

sanskrit: a̱yaṁ vṛta̍ś cātayate samī̱cīr ya ā̱jiṣu̍ ma̱ghavā̍ śṛ̱ṇva eka̍ḥ | a̱yaṁ vāja̍m bharati̱ yaṁ sa̱noty a̱sya pri̱yāsa̍ḥ sa̱khye syā̍ma ||
english: He, the chosen one, repels the hostile throngs — the Maghavan who alone is heard in the contests. He brings the prize-reward to him whom he favors; may we be dear friends in his companionship.

sanskrit: a̱yaṁ śṛ̍ṇve̱ adha̱ jaya̍nn u̱ta ghnann a̱yam u̱ta pra kṛ̍ṇute yu̱dhā gāḥ | ya̱dā sa̱tyaṁ kṛ̍ṇu̱te ma̱nyum indro̱ viśva̍ṁ dṛ̱ḻham bha̍yata̱ eja̍d asmāt ||
english: This one is heard while conquering and while slaying; he wins the cows in battle. Whenever Indra makes his fury real, everything firm trembles and shakes away from him.

sanskrit: sam indro̱ gā a̍jaya̱t saṁ hira̍ṇyā̱ sam a̍śvi̱yā ma̱ghavā̱ yo ha̍ pū̱rvīḥ | e̱bhir nṛbhi̱r nṛta̍mo asya śā̱kai rā̱yo vi̍bha̱ktā sa̍mbha̱raś ca̱ vasva̍ḥ ||
english: Indra won the cows together, the gold together, the horses together — the Maghavan of many of old. With these men, through the manliest one's capabilities, wealth is distributed and goods are gathered.

sanskrit: kiya̍t svi̱d indro̱ adhy e̍ti mā̱tuḥ kiya̍t pi̱tur ja̍ni̱tur yo ja̱jāna̍ | yo a̍sya̱ śuṣma̍m muhu̱kair iya̍rti̱ vāto̱ na jū̱taḥ sta̱naya̍dbhir a̱bhraiḥ ||
english: How far does Indra excel his mother? How far the father who begot him? He who drives his vigor with sudden bursts, like wind spurred on by thundering clouds.

sanskrit: kṣi̱yanta̍ṁ tva̱m akṣi̍yantaṁ kṛṇo̱tīya̍rti re̱ṇum ma̱ghavā̍ sa̱moha̍m | vi̱bha̱ñja̱nur a̱śani̍mām̐ iva̱ dyaur u̱ta sto̱tāra̍m ma̱ghavā̱ vasau̍ dhāt ||
english: The Maghavan makes the perishing one imperishable; he stirs up the dust all at once. Like heaven shattering the cloud with his bolt, the Maghavan sets the praiser among good things.

sanskrit: a̱yaṁ ca̱kram i̍ṣaṇa̱t sūrya̍sya̱ ny eta̍śaṁ rīramat sasṛmā̱ṇam | ā kṛ̱ṣṇa ī̍ṁ juhurā̱ṇo ji̍gharti tva̱co bu̱dhne raja̍so a̱sya yonau̍ ||
english: He set the sun's wheel rolling; he halted Etaśa, who had been running. The dark one, spurting, licks the base of heaven's skin at the bottom of this atmosphere.

sanskrit: asi̍knyā̱ṁ yaja̍māno̱ na hotā̍ ||
english: Like a sacrificer at the Asiknī — like a hotar priest.

sanskrit: ga̱vyanta̱ indra̍ṁ sa̱khyāya̱ viprā̍ aśvā̱yanto̱ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ vā̱jaya̍ntaḥ | ja̱nī̱yanto̍ jani̱dām akṣi̍toti̱m ā cyā̍vayāmo 'va̱te na kośa̍m ||
english: Desiring cattle, desiring friendship with Indra, desiring horses and seeking victory over the bull, desiring offspring from the giver of offspring and of inexhaustible help — we urge him down like the bucket in the well.

sanskrit: trā̱tā no̍ bodhi̱ dadṛ̍śāna ā̱pir a̍bhikhyā̱tā ma̍rḍi̱tā so̱myānā̍m | sakhā̍ pi̱tā pi̱tṛta̍maḥ pitṝ̱ṇāṁ karte̍m u lo̱kam u̍śa̱te va̍yo̱dhāḥ ||
english: Be our visible protector, our ally, our famous comforter of soma-offerers — a companion, a father, the most fatherly of fathers; and fashion a world for one who desires — the bestower of strength.

sanskrit: sa̱khī̱ya̱tām a̍vi̱tā bo̍dhi̱ sakhā̍ gṛṇā̱na i̍ndra stuva̱te vayo̍ dhāḥ ||
english: Seeking friendship, be a protector, be a companion — praised, O Indra, bestow strength on the one who praises. We have greatly glorified you with these worship-acts, O Indra.

sanskrit: stu̱ta indro̍ ma̱ghavā̱ yad dha̍ vṛ̱trā bhūrī̱ṇy eko̍ apra̱tīni̍ hanti | a̱sya pri̱yo ja̍ri̱tā yasya̱ śarma̱n naki̍r de̱vā vā̱raya̍nte̱ na martā̍ḥ ||
english: Praised, the bountiful Indra slays many irresistible Vṛtras alone. The praiser who is dear to him — in whose shelter neither gods nor mortals obstruct him.

sanskrit: e̱vā na̱ indro̍ ma̱ghavā̍ vira̱pśī kara̍t sa̱tyā ca̍rṣaṇī̱dhṛd a̍na̱rvā | tvaṁ rājā̍ ja̱nuṣā̍ṁ dhehy a̱sme adhi̱ śravo̱ māhi̍na̱ṁ yaj ja̍ri̱tre ||
english: Thus let bountiful Indra, the mighty, wide-ranging sustainer of peoples, perform true deeds — unchecked. You are king of creatures; establish upon us the great glory that belongs to the one who praises you.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: a̱yam panthā̱ anu̍vittaḥ purā̱ṇo yato̍ de̱vā u̱dajā̍yanta̱ viśve̍ | ata̍ś ci̱d ā ja̍niṣīṣṭa̱ pravṛ̍ddho̱ mā mā̱tara̍m amu̱yā patta̍ve kaḥ ||
english: This ancient path has been found — from which all the gods were born. From here even the greatly swollen one must be born; let none make the mother stumble like that.

sanskrit: nāham ato̱ nir a̍yā du̱rgahai̱tat ti̱ra̱ścatā̍ pā̱rśvān nir ga̍māṇi | ba̱hūni̍ me̱ akṛ̍tā̱ kartvā̍ni̱ yudhyai̍ tvena̱ saṁ tve̍na pṛcchai ||
english: I will not go out from here by the difficult passage — let me go out sideways through the flanks. Many things I have still to do: I shall fight with this one, and debate with this one.

sanskrit: pa̱rā̱ya̱tīm mā̱tara̱m anv a̍caṣṭa̱ na nānu̍ gā̱ny anu̱ nū ga̍māni | tvaṣṭu̍r gṛ̱he a̍piba̱t soma̱m indra̍ḥ śatadha̱nya̍ṁ ca̱mvo̍ḥ su̱tasya̍ ||
english: He watched his mother departing — 'Shall I not follow the paths? Shall I follow now?' In the house of Tvaṣṭṛ, Indra drank the soma — the hundredfold pressed from the bowls.

sanskrit: kiṁ sa ṛdha̍k kṛṇava̱d yaṁ sa̱hasra̍m mā̱so ja̱bhāra̍ śa̱rada̍ś ca pū̱rvīḥ | na̱hī nv a̍sya prati̱māna̱m asty a̱ntar jā̱teṣū̱ta ye jani̍tvāḥ ||
english: What could he accomplish separately — he whom a thousand months and many autumns carried? For indeed there is no equal to him among those born or those yet to be born.

sanskrit: a̱va̱dyam i̍va̱ manya̍mānā̱ guhā̍ka̱r indra̍m mā̱tā vī̱rye̍ṇā̱ nyṛ̍ṣṭam | athod a̍sthāt sva̱yam atka̱ṁ vasā̍na̱ ā roda̍sī apṛṇā̱j jāya̍mānaḥ ||
english: His mother, thinking him as it were defective, hid Indra who had been impelled by his vigor. But then he stood up of himself, donning his garment — being born, he filled the two world-halves.

sanskrit: e̱tā a̍rṣanty alalā̱bhava̍ntīr ṛ̱tāva̍rīr iva sa̱ṁkrośa̍mānāḥ | e̱tā vi pṛ̍ccha̱ kim i̱dam bha̍nanti̱ kam āpo̱ adri̍m pari̱dhiṁ ru̍janti ||
english: These flow on with a rushing sound, crying out like those who hold ṛta together. Ask them what it is they declare — which rock-enclosure do the waters break through?

sanskrit: kim u̍ ṣvid asmai ni̱vido̍ bhana̱ntendra̍syāva̱dyaṁ di̍dhiṣanta̱ āpa̍ḥ | mamai̱tān pu̱tro ma̍ha̱tā va̱dhena̍ vṛ̱traṁ ja̍gha̱nvām̐ a̍sṛja̱d vi sindhū̍n ||
english: What then do these speeches declare, seeking to reproach Indra — these waters? 'My son, having slain Vṛtra with a great weapon, set free these very rivers.'

sanskrit: mama̍c ca̱na tvā̍ yuva̱tiḥ pa̱rāsa̱ mama̍c ca̱na tvā̍ ku̱ṣavā̍ ja̱gāra̍ | mama̍c ci̱d āpa̱ḥ śiśa̍ve mamṛḍyu̱r mama̍c ci̱d indra̱ḥ saha̱sod a̍tiṣṭhat ||
english: No young woman abandoned you — no; the Kuṣavā did not swallow you. No: even the waters were kind to the child; no: even then Indra stood up with power.

sanskrit: mama̍c ca̱na te̍ maghava̱n vya̍ṁso nivivi̱dhvām̐ apa̱ hanū̍ ja̱ghāna̍ | adhā̱ nivi̍ddha̱ utta̍ro babhū̱vāñ chiro̍ dā̱sasya̱ sam pi̍ṇag va̱dhena̍ ||
english: No: for your shoulder-blades, O Maghavan — he struck the jaw of the one who had pierced through them. Then, with the pierced one overcome, he crushed the Dāsa's head with his weapon.

sanskrit: gṛ̱ṣṭiḥ sa̍sūva̱ sthavi̍raṁ tavā̱gām a̍nādhṛ̱ṣyaṁ vṛ̍ṣa̱bhaṁ tumra̱m indra̍m | arī̍ḻhaṁ va̱tsaṁ ca̱rathā̍ya mā̱tā sva̱yaṁ gā̱tuṁ ta̱nva̍ i̱cchamā̍nam ||
english: The cow gave birth to you, the strong-arrived one, the indomitable bull, the robust Indra — the unlicked calf, the mother let him go his own way, himself seeking his body's own path.

sanskrit: u̱ta mā̱tā ma̍hi̱ṣam anv a̍venad a̱mī tvā̍ jahati putra de̱vāḥ | athā̍bravīd vṛ̱tram indro̍ hani̱ṣyan sakhe̍ viṣṇo vita̱raṁ vi kra̍masva ||
english: And the mother followed after the great bull — 'These gods, O son, are abandoning you.' Then said Indra, about to slay Vṛtra: 'O friend Viṣṇu, stride forth widely.'

sanskrit: kas te̍ mā̱tara̍ṁ vi̱dhavā̍m acakrac cha̱yuṁ kas tvām a̍jighāṁsa̱c cara̍ntam | kas te̍ de̱vo adhi̍ mārḍī̱ka ā̍sī̱d yat prākṣi̍ṇāḥ pi̱tara̍m pāda̱gṛhya̍ ||
english: Who made your mother a widow while resting? Who tried to slay you while you moved about? Which god was your protector above when you seized your father by the foot and crushed him?

sanskrit: ava̍rtyā̱ śuna̍ ā̱ntrāṇi̍ pece̱ na de̱veṣu̍ vivide marḍi̱tāra̍m | apa̍śyaṁ jā̱yām ama̍hīyamānā̱m adhā̍ me śye̱no madhv ā ja̍bhāra ||
english: He cooked the intestines of a dog in need — he found no comforter among the gods. I saw my wife dishonored; then a falcon brought me the soma-honey.

sanskrit: e̱vā tvām i̍ndra vajri̱nn atra̱ viśve̍ de̱vāsa̍ḥ su̱havā̍sa̱ ūmā̍ḥ | ma̱hām u̱bhe roda̍sī vṛ̱ddham ṛ̱ṣvaṁ nir eka̱m id vṛ̍ṇate vṛtra̱hatye̍ ||
english: Thus, O Indra, O wielder of the bolt, all the gods, easy to invoke, helpers — they choose you alone, the great, elevated, grown one, for the slaying of Vṛtra in both worlds.

sanskrit: avā̍sṛjanta̱ jivra̍yo̱ na de̱vā bhuva̍ḥ sa̱mrāḻ i̍ndra sa̱tyayo̍niḥ | aha̱nn ahi̍m pari̱śayā̍na̱m arṇa̱ḥ pra va̍rta̱nīr a̍rado vi̱śvadhe̍nāḥ ||
english: The gods released you like swift ones; you became, O Indra, sovereign, of true birth. You slew the serpent lying around the flood; you set rolling the all-nourishing paths.

sanskrit: atṛ̍pṇuvanta̱ṁ viya̍tam abu̱dhyam abu̍dhyamānaṁ suṣupā̱ṇam i̍ndra | sa̱pta prati̍ pra̱vata̍ ā̱śayā̍na̱m ahi̱ṁ vajre̍ṇa̱ vi ri̍ṇā apa̱rvan ||
english: Him who was insatiate, dispersed, not awake, sleeping deep and unaware — O Indra, you split apart with the bolt the seven-jointed serpent lying on the downward slope.

sanskrit: akṣo̍daya̱c chava̍sā̱ kṣāma̍ bu̱dhnaṁ vār ṇa vāta̱s tavi̍ṣībhi̱r indra̍ḥ | dṛ̱ḻhāny au̍bhnād u̱śamā̍na̱ oja 'vā̍bhinat ka̱kubha̱ḥ parva̍tānām ||
english: Indra shook the earth to its foundation by his might, like wind with its powers over the water. Eager in his strength he burst open the strong things; he split the mountain peaks asunder.

sanskrit: a̱bhi pra da̍dru̱r jana̍yo̱ na garbha̱ṁ rathā̍ iva̱ pra ya̍yuḥ sā̱kam adra̍yaḥ | ata̍rpayo vi̱sṛta̍ u̱bja ū̱rmīn tvaṁ vṛ̱tām̐ a̍riṇā indra̱ sindhū̍n ||
english: They rushed forward like women to the embryo; the stones rolled forward together like chariots. You satisfied the released, upward-surging waves — you set the obstructed rivers free, O Indra.

sanskrit: tvam ma̱hīm a̱vani̍ṁ vi̱śvadhe̍nāṁ tu̱rvīta̍ye va̱yyā̍ya̱ kṣara̍ntīm | ara̍mayo̱ nama̱saija̱d arṇa̍ḥ sutara̱ṇām̐ a̍kṛṇor indra̱ sindhū̍n ||
english: You set flowing the great, all-nourishing earth for Turvīta and Vayya. With homage the enemies trembled; you made the rivers, O Indra, easy to cross.

sanskrit: prāgruvo̍ nabha̱nvo̱3̱̍ na vakvā̍ dhva̱srā a̍pinvad yuva̱tīr ṛ̍ta̱jñāḥ ||
english: Like the rushing, bursting forward, murmuring of the cloud, he filled the young women who know ṛta — the gleaming ones. He filled the deserts and plains, thirsting; Indra milked the cows that have strength as their mates.

sanskrit: pū̱rvīr u̱ṣasa̍ḥ śa̱rada̍ś ca gū̱rtā vṛ̱traṁ ja̍gha̱nvām̐ a̍sṛja̱d vi sindhū̍n | pari̍ṣṭhitā atṛṇad badbadhā̱nāḥ sī̱rā indra̱ḥ sravi̍tave pṛthi̱vyā ||
english: Through many welcome dawns and autumns, having slain Vṛtra, he set the rivers free. He mowed down those that were stopped up, repeatedly bound — Indra cut the furrows to flow for the earth.

sanskrit: va̱mrībhi̍ḥ pu̱tram a̱gruvo̍ adā̱naṁ ni̱veśa̍nād dhariva̱ ā ja̍bhartha | vy a1̱̍ndho a̍khya̱d ahi̍m ādadā̱no nir bhū̍d ukha̱cchit sam a̍ranta̱ parva̍ ||
english: From the ant-hill you, O lord of tawny steeds, brought forth the son of Agruva, the ungiven one from his dwelling. The blind one saw the serpent when taking it; the pot-sherd broke out; the joints came together.

sanskrit: pra te̱ pūrvā̍ṇi̱ kara̍ṇāni viprāvi̱dvām̐ ā̍ha vi̱duṣe̱ karā̍ṁsi | yathā̍-yathā̱ vṛṣṇyā̍ni̱ svagū̱rtāpā̍ṁsi rāja̱n naryāvi̍veṣīḥ ||
english: An inspired poet, knowing, declares your ancient deeds to the knowing — what he will do. In whatever manner, O king, you displayed your welcomed, manly, virile water-works.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: ā na̱ indro̍ dū̱rād ā na̍ ā̱sād a̍bhiṣṭi̱kṛd ava̍se yāsad u̱graḥ | oji̍ṣṭhebhir nṛ̱pati̱r vajra̍bāhuḥ sa̱ṁge sa̱matsu̍ tu̱rvaṇi̍ḥ pṛta̱nyūn ||
english: Let Indra come to us from afar, come near to us — the fierce one who creates invincibility — to be our aid. The lord of men with the bolt-arm and his mightiest companions: the swift conqueror of enemies in meetings and battles.

sanskrit: ā na̱ indro̱ hari̍bhir yā̱tv acchā̍rvācī̱no 'va̍se̱ rādha̍se ca | tiṣṭhā̍ti va̱jrī ma̱ghavā̍ vira̱pśīmaṁ ya̱jñam anu̍ no̱ vāja̍sātau ||
english: Let Indra come toward us with his tawny steeds, facing this way, for our aid and for bounty. Let the bolt-bearer stand by — the bountiful, mighty one — following this sacrifice of ours for the winning of prizes.

sanskrit: i̱maṁ ya̱jñaṁ tvam a̱smāka̍m indra pu̱ro dadha̍t saniṣyasi̱ kratu̍ṁ naḥ | śva̱ghnīva̍ vajrin sa̱naye̱ dhanā̍nā̱ṁ tvayā̍ va̱yam a̱rya ā̱jiṁ ja̍yema ||
english: Placing this sacrifice of ours at the fore, O Indra, you shall win our intention. Like a dice player for the winning of wealth, O bolt-bearer — with you, O lord, may we win the contest.

sanskrit: u̱śann u̱ ṣu ṇa̍ḥ su̱manā̍ upā̱ke soma̍sya̱ nu suṣu̍tasya svadhāvaḥ | pā i̍ndra̱ prati̍bhṛtasya̱ madhva̱ḥ sam andha̍sā mamadaḥ pṛ̱ṣṭhye̍na ||
english: Come willing, benevolent, near to us — now of the well-pressed soma, O self-abiding one. Drink, O Indra, of the proffered honey-sweet; be fully intoxicated with the food placed on the back.

sanskrit: vi yo ra̍ra̱pśa ṛṣi̍bhi̱r nave̍bhir vṛ̱kṣo na pa̱kvaḥ sṛṇyo̱ na jetā̍ | maryo̱ na yoṣā̍m a̱bhi manya̍mā̱no 'cchā̍ vivakmi puruhū̱tam indra̍m ||
english: He who is acclaimed with new poets — like a ripened tree, like a triumphant fighter — like a young man thinking toward women: toward the much-invoked Indra I speak forth.

sanskrit: gi̱rir na yaḥ svata̍vām̐ ṛ̱ṣva indra̍ḥ sa̱nād e̱va saha̍se jā̱ta u̱graḥ ||
english: Like a mountain mighty in its own strength — the elevated Indra, from ancient time alone born for might — the fierce one. Who holds the bolt in his arms, eager — like a full vessel stocked with goods.

sanskrit: na yasya̍ va̱rtā ja̱nuṣā̱ nv asti̱ na rādha̍sa āmarī̱tā ma̱ghasya̍ | u̱dvā̱vṛ̱ṣā̱ṇas ta̍viṣīva ugrā̱smabhya̍ṁ daddhi puruhūta rā̱yaḥ ||
english: He has no equal by birth, none who has consumed the bounty of his gift. Bellowing upward in his strength — fierce — give us wealth, O much-invoked one.

sanskrit: īkṣe̍ rā̱yaḥ kṣaya̍sya carṣaṇī̱nām u̱ta vra̱jam a̍pava̱rtāsi̱ gonā̍m | śi̱kṣā̱na̱raḥ sa̍mi̱theṣu̍ pra̱hāvā̱n vasvo̍ rā̱śim a̍bhine̱tāsi̱ bhūri̍m ||
english: I look toward wealth, toward the dominion of peoples; you turn away also the pen of the cow-herds. You who teach men at meetings, ready for battle — you lead toward a great heap of riches.

sanskrit: kayā̱ tac chṛ̍ṇve̱ śacyā̱ śaci̍ṣṭho̱ yayā̍ kṛ̱ṇoti̱ muhu̱ kā ci̍d ṛ̱ṣvaḥ | pu̱ru dā̱śuṣe̱ vica̍yiṣṭho̱ aṁho 'thā̍ dadhāti̱ dravi̍ṇaṁ jari̱tre ||
english: By what power is the most powerful one heard — by which the lofty one, whatever it may be, keeps making actions suddenly? He who most abundantly wards off distress from the generous worshiper — then he bestows wealth on the praiser.

sanskrit: mā no̍ mardhī̱r ā bha̍rā da̱ddhi tan na̱ḥ pra dā̱śuṣe̱ dāta̍ve̱ bhūri̱ yat te̍ | navye̍ de̱ṣṇe śa̱ste a̱smin ta̍ u̱kthe pra bra̍vāma va̱yam i̍ndra stu̱vanta̍ḥ ||
english: Do not neglect us — bring it, give that abundance of yours to the generous man to give. In this praised, fresh gift — your lauded one — we speak forth, O Indra, as praisers.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: ā yā̱tv indro 'va̍sa̱ upa̍ na i̱ha stu̱taḥ sa̍dha̱mād a̍stu̱ śūra̍ḥ | vā̱vṛ̱dhā̱nas tavi̍ṣī̱r yasya̍ pū̱rvīr dyaur na kṣa̱tram a̱bhibhū̍ti̱ puṣyā̍t ||
english: Let Indra come here to us for aid — let the hero be here praised, exulting in the feast. Having grown strong through his many powers, may his dominion spread like heaven's overwhelming rule.

sanskrit: tasyed i̱ha sta̍vatha̱ vṛṣṇyā̍ni tuvidyu̱mnasya̍ tuvi̱rādha̍so̱ nṝn | yasya̱ kratu̍r vida̱thyo̱3̱̍ na sa̱mrāṭ sā̱hvān taru̍tro a̱bhy asti̍ kṛ̱ṣṭīḥ ||
english: Here laud his virile deeds — those of the much-glorious, richly-bountiful one, lord of men — whose will, like a king at the assembly, as a triumphant conqueror overpowers the peoples.

sanskrit: ā yā̱tv indro̍ di̱va ā pṛ̍thi̱vyā ma̱kṣū sa̍mu̱drād u̱ta vā̱ purī̍ṣāt | sva̍rṇarā̱d ava̍se no ma̱rutvā̍n parā̱vato̍ vā̱ sada̍nād ṛ̱tasya̍ ||
english: Let Indra come to us from heaven, from earth, swiftly from the ocean or from the fullness — with the Maruts, for our aid, from the radiant realm of men, or from the far-off seat of ṛta.

sanskrit: sthū̱rasya̍ rā̱yo bṛ̍ha̱to ya īśe̱ tam u̍ ṣṭavāma vi̱dathe̱ṣv indra̍m | yo vā̱yunā̱ jaya̍ti̱ goma̍tīṣu̱ pra dhṛ̍ṣṇu̱yā naya̍ti̱ vasyo̱ accha̍ ||
english: Of the firm and great wealth who is the lord — him indeed we shall praise at the assemblies — Indra, who wins among cattle-rich hosts through Vāyu, and leads boldly toward better things.

sanskrit: upa̱ yo namo̱ nama̍si stabhā̱yann iya̍rti̱ vāca̍ṁ ja̱naya̱n yaja̍dhyai | ṛ̱ñja̱sā̱naḥ pu̍ru̱vāra̍ u̱kthair endra̍ṁ kṛṇvīta̱ sada̍neṣu̱ hotā̍ ||
english: He who, establishing himself in homage upon homage, sets the speech in motion to generate worship — rightly directed, with abundant choice lauds, let the hotar priest make Indra present at the seatings.

sanskrit: dhi̱ṣā yadi̍ dhiṣa̱ṇyanta̍ḥ sara̱ṇyān sada̍nto̱ adri̍m auśi̱jasya̱ gohe̍ | ā du̱roṣā̍ḥ pā̱styasya̱ hotā̱ yo no̍ ma̱hān sa̱ṁvara̍ṇeṣu̱ vahni̍ḥ ||
english: When with inspired thought the thinkers — sitting hard-pressed, pressing the stone — in the cow-stable of Auśija: the house-fire of the dwelling as hotar — he who is the great carrier for us at the enclosures.

sanskrit: sa̱trā yad ī̍m bhārva̱rasya̱ vṛṣṇa̱ḥ siṣa̍kti̱ śuṣma̍ḥ stuva̱te bharā̍ya | guhā̱ yad ī̍m auśi̱jasya̱ gohe̱ pra yad dhi̱ye prāya̍se̱ madā̍ya ||
english: When indeed the virile force of Bhārvara entirely accompanies the praiser for bringing — when in the hidden cow-stable of Auśija, when for thought's journey toward intoxication.

sanskrit: vi yad varā̍ṁsi̱ parva̍tasya vṛ̱ṇve payo̍bhir ji̱nve a̱pāṁ javā̍ṁsi | vi̱dad gau̱rasya̍ gava̱yasya̱ gohe̱ yadī̱ vājā̍ya su̱dhyo̱3̱̍ vaha̍nti ||
english: When he covers over the mountain-flanks, refreshes with milk-streams the swiftness of the waters, finds the wild bull and gayal in their pen — when the well-minded ones carry for the prize.

sanskrit: bha̱drā te̱ hastā̱ sukṛ̍to̱ta pā̱ṇī pra̍ya̱ntārā̍ stuva̱te rādha̍ indra | kā te̱ niṣa̍tti̱ḥ kim u̱ no ma̍matsi̱ kiṁ nod-u̍d u harṣase̱ dāta̱vā u̍ ||
english: Good are your hands, well-made, your palms — bestowing bounty, O Indra, upon the one who praises. What is your sitting-place? For what do you delight in us? For what do you exult when there is something to give?

sanskrit: e̱vā vasva̱ indra̍ḥ sa̱tyaḥ sa̱mrāḍ ḍhantā̍ vṛ̱traṁ vari̍vaḥ pū̱rave̍ kaḥ | puru̍ṣṭuta̱ kratvā̍ naḥ śagdhi rā̱yo bha̍kṣī̱ya te 'va̍so̱ daivya̍sya ||
english: Thus is Indra: true, sovereign lord of wealth — the slayer of Vṛtra who made broad space for Pūru. O much-praised one, through your will be capable of giving us wealth; may I partake of your divine aid.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: yan na̱ indro̍ juju̱ṣe yac ca̱ vaṣṭi̱ tan no̍ ma̱hān ka̍rati śu̱ṣmy ā ci̍t | brahma̱ stoma̍m ma̱ghavā̱ soma̍m u̱kthā yo aśmā̍na̱ṁ śava̍sā̱ bibhra̱d eti̍ ||
english: What Indra has enjoyed and what he desires — that let the great, even the mighty one do for us. The prayer, the hymn, the bountiful one, the soma, the laud — he who bearing the stone goes with might.

sanskrit: vṛṣā̱ vṛṣa̍ndhi̱ṁ catu̍raśri̱m asya̍nn u̱gro bā̱hubhyā̱ṁ nṛta̍ma̱ḥ śacī̍vān | śri̱ye paru̍ṣṇīm u̱ṣamā̍ṇa̱ ūrṇā̱ṁ yasyā̱ḥ parvā̍ṇi sa̱khyāya̍ vi̱vye ||
english: The bull hurling the four-square bolted udder — the fierce one, most manly with both arms, powerful. Glowing with beauty he wrapped the Paruṣṇī in wool, whose joints he covered over for friendship.

sanskrit: yo de̱vo de̱vata̍mo̱ jāya̍māno ma̱ho vāje̍bhir ma̱hadbhi̍ś ca̱ śuṣmai̍ḥ | dadhā̍no̱ vajra̍m bā̱hvor u̱śanta̱ṁ dyām ame̍na rejaya̱t pra bhūma̍ ||
english: The god who, being born, is most god-like — with great prizes and great forces — holding the eager bolt in his arms, he shook heaven and earth with his rush.

sanskrit: viśvā̱ rodhā̍ṁsi pra̱vata̍ś ca pū̱rvīr dyaur ṛ̱ṣvāj jani̍man rejata̱ kṣāḥ | ā mā̱tarā̱ bhara̍ti śu̱ṣmy ā gor nṛ̱vat pari̍jman nonuvanta̱ vātā̍ḥ ||
english: All obstructions and many slopes trembled — heaven at the elevated birth, the earth. The mighty one brings both mother-cows; the winds resounded with a manly roaring on every side.

sanskrit: tā tū ta̍ indra maha̱to ma̱hāni̱ viśve̱ṣv it sava̍neṣu pra̱vācyā̍ | yac chū̍ra dhṛṣṇo dhṛṣa̱tā da̍dhṛ̱ṣvān ahi̱ṁ vajre̍ṇa̱ śava̱sāvi̍veṣīḥ ||
english: These great deeds of yours, O great Indra, are truly to be proclaimed at all pressings — when, O hero, O bold one, holding boldly, you drove the serpent through with your bolt by your might.

sanskrit: tā tū te̍ sa̱tyā tu̍vinṛmṇa̱ viśvā̱ pra dhe̱nava̍ḥ sisrate̱ vṛṣṇa̱ ūdhna̍ḥ | adhā̍ ha̱ tvad vṛ̍ṣamaṇo bhiyā̱nāḥ pra sindha̍vo̱ java̍sā cakramanta ||
english: These are truly yours, of great might — all the cows flow forth from the virile udder. Then, indeed, afraid of you, the Vṛṣamaṇa peoples: the rivers strode forward in their swiftness.

sanskrit: atrāha̍ te hariva̱s tā u̍ de̱vīr avo̍bhir indra stavanta̱ svasā̍raḥ | yat sī̱m anu̱ pra mu̱co ba̍dbadhā̱nā dī̱rghām anu̱ prasi̍tiṁ syanda̱yadhyai̍ ||
english: Here, O lord of tawny steeds, those divine sisters praise you with their aids, O Indra — in that you set them free along their course, the repeatedly bound ones, to stream along a long path.

sanskrit: pi̱pī̱ḻe a̱ṁśur madyo̱ na sindhu̱r ā tvā̱ śamī̍ śaśamā̱nasya̍ śa̱ktiḥ ||
english: The intoxicating soma-stalk has swelled like a river — the diligence of the one striving comes to you, the strength. From our side, the gleaming one blazing — the track of the bull's powerful one — a swift beam to the cow.

sanskrit: a̱sme varṣi̍ṣṭhā kṛṇuhi̱ jyeṣṭhā̍ nṛ̱mṇāni̍ sa̱trā sa̍hure̱ sahā̍ṁsi | a̱smabhya̍ṁ vṛ̱trā su̱hanā̍ni randhi ja̱hi vadha̍r va̱nuṣo̱ martya̍sya ||
english: Make for us the highest and greatest manly powers — together, O overwhelming one, the might-powers. Grant to us the Vṛtras easy to slay; strike down the weapon of the greedy mortal.

sanskrit: a̱smāka̱m it su śṛ̍ṇuhi̱ tvam i̍ndrā̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱trām̐ upa̍ māhi̱ vājā̍n | a̱smabhya̱ṁ viśvā̍ iṣaṇa̱ḥ pura̍ṁdhīr a̱smāka̱ṁ su ma̍ghavan bodhi go̱dāḥ ||
english: Do well hear us, O Indra — measure brilliant prizes toward us. Set in motion for us all the bountiful thoughts; be well, O Maghavan, our giver of cattle.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: ka̱thā ma̱hām a̍vṛdha̱t kasya̱ hotu̍r ya̱jñaṁ ju̍ṣā̱ṇo a̱bhi soma̱m ūdha̍ḥ | piba̍nn uśā̱no ju̱ṣamā̍ṇo̱ andho̍ vava̱kṣa ṛ̱ṣvaḥ śu̍ca̱te dhanā̍ya ||
english: How did the great one grow? Enjoying the sacrifice of which hotar, approaching the soma-udder? Drinking, desiring, enjoying the soma-food, the lofty one has swelled for the gleaming prize.

sanskrit: ko a̍sya vī̱raḥ sa̍dha̱māda̍m āpa̱ sam ā̍naṁśa suma̱tibhi̱ḥ ko a̍sya | kad a̍sya ci̱traṁ ci̍kite̱ kad ū̱tī vṛ̱dhe bhu̍vac chaśamā̱nasya̱ yajyo̍ḥ ||
english: Which hero has attained his feast-sharing? Who has grasped his good thoughts? What brilliant deed of his is perceived? What aid may there be for the growth of the one striving, who is worthy of worship?

sanskrit: ka̱thā śṛ̍ṇoti hū̱yamā̍na̱m indra̍ḥ ka̱thā śṛ̱ṇvann ava̍sām asya veda | kā a̍sya pū̱rvīr upa̍mātayo ha ka̱thaina̍m āhu̱ḥ papu̍riṁ jari̱tre ||
english: How does Indra hear when being called? Hearing, how does he know his aids? What are his many comparisons? How do they call him the drinker among praisers?

sanskrit: ka̱thā sa̱bādha̍ḥ śaśamā̱no a̍sya̱ naśa̍d a̱bhi dravi̍ṇa̱ṁ dīdhyā̍naḥ | de̱vo bhu̍va̱n nave̍dā ma ṛ̱tānā̱ṁ namo̍ jagṛ̱bhvām̐ a̱bhi yaj jujo̍ṣat ||
english: How does the hard-pressed one who strives attain his wealth, pondering? The god has become the knower of my ṛta-truths — he takes hold of homage and enjoys what he worships.

sanskrit: ka̱thā kad a̱syā u̱ṣaso̱ vyu̍ṣṭau de̱vo marta̍sya sa̱khyaṁ ju̍joṣa | ka̱thā kad a̍sya sa̱khyaṁ sakhi̍bhyo̱ ye a̍smi̱n kāma̍ṁ su̱yuja̍ṁ tata̱sre ||
english: How and when at the shining forth of this dawn does the god enjoy the mortal's friendship? How and when does his friendship extend to those companions who have stretched out toward him the well-yoked desire?

sanskrit: kim ād ama̍traṁ sa̱khyaṁ sakhi̍bhyaḥ ka̱dā nu te̍ bhrā̱tram pra bra̍vāma | śri̱ye su̱dṛśo̱ vapu̍r asya̱ sargā̱ḥ sva1̱̍r ṇa ci̱trata̍mam iṣa̱ ā goḥ ||
english: What then is the boundless friendship for his companions? When shall we speak of your brotherhood? His releasing streams are of fair form for beauty — like brilliant heaven in the refreshment of the cow.

sanskrit: druha̱ṁ jighā̍ṁsan dhva̱rasa̍m ani̱ndrāṁ teti̍kte ti̱gmā tu̱jase̱ anī̍kā | ṛ̱ṇā ci̱d yatra̍ ṛṇa̱yā na̍ u̱gro dū̱re ajñā̍tā u̱ṣaso̍ babā̱dhe ||
english: Seeking to slay deceit, the curved, the Indra-less — the sharp battle-faces are whetted to smite. Even where the fierce one strikes at the debts with debt-obliterating — far off, pushing back the unknown dawns.

sanskrit: ṛ̱tasya̱ hi śu̱rudha̱ḥ santi̍ pū̱rvīr ṛ̱tasya̍ dhī̱tir vṛ̍ji̱nāni̍ hanti | ṛ̱tasya̱ śloko̍ badhi̱rā ta̍tarda̱ karṇā̍ budhā̱naḥ śu̱camā̍na ā̱yoḥ ||
english: For ṛta has many streams of nourishment; the thought of ṛta smites crooked things. The resonance of ṛta has pierced even the deaf ears — awakening, illuminating the lifespan of man.

sanskrit: ṛ̱tasya̍ dṛ̱ḻhā dha̱ruṇā̍ni santi pu̱rūṇi̍ ca̱ndrā vapu̍ṣe̱ vapū̍ṁṣi | ṛ̱tena̍ dī̱rgham i̍ṣaṇanta̱ pṛkṣa̍ ṛ̱tena̱ gāva̍ ṛ̱tam ā vi̍veśuḥ ||
english: The firm foundations of ṛta exist — many gleaming forms for beauty. By ṛta the nourishments press far and long; by ṛta the cows have entered into ṛta.

sanskrit: ṛ̱taṁ ye̍mā̱na ṛ̱tam id va̍noty ṛ̱tasya̱ śuṣma̍s tura̱yā u̍ ga̱vyuḥ ||
english: He who holds ṛta in order gains ṛta alone; the force of ṛta is swift and seeks the cattle. For ṛta the broad, deep earth — for ṛta the two supreme cows are milked.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: kā su̍ṣṭu̱tiḥ śava̍saḥ sū̱num indra̍m arvācī̱naṁ rādha̍sa̱ ā va̍vartat | da̱dir hi vī̱ro gṛ̍ṇa̱te vasū̍ni̱ sa gopa̍tir ni̱ṣṣidhā̍ṁ no janāsaḥ ||
english: What excellent praise has turned the son of might — Indra — hither toward bounty? The hero gives goods to the one who praises him; he is the lord of the herd — let him, O people, drive away our obstacles.

sanskrit: sa vṛ̍tra̱hatye̱ havya̱ḥ sa īḍya̱ḥ sa suṣṭu̍ta̱ indra̍ḥ sa̱tyarā̍dhāḥ | sa yāma̱nn ā ma̱ghavā̱ martyā̍ya brahmaṇya̱te suṣva̍ye̱ vari̍vo dhāt ||
english: He is to be called upon at the slaying of Vṛtra; he is to be praised — the truly bountiful Indra, well-lauded. He who, on his course, O Maghavan, for the mortal who prays and presses well, establishes broad space.

sanskrit: tam in naro̱ vi hva̍yante samī̱ke ri̍ri̱kvāṁsa̍s ta̱nva̍ḥ kṛṇvata̱ trām | mi̱tho yat tyā̱gam u̱bhayā̍so̱ agma̱n nara̍s to̱kasya̱ tana̍yasya sā̱tau ||
english: Him men call forth variously in battle — those who have left behind their bodies making a shield. When both parties have met the mutual abandonment — men in the winning of offspring and progeny.

sanskrit: kra̱tū̱yanti̍ kṣi̱tayo̱ yoga̍ ugrāśuṣā̱ṇāso̍ mi̱tho arṇa̍sātau | saṁ yad viśo 'va̍vṛtranta yu̱dhmā ād in nema̍ indrayante a̱bhīke̍ ||
english: The peoples exert their wills in the fierce yoking — eager for mutual flood-winning. When the warrior clans turn against each other in battle, then these ones make Indra their concern in the encounter.

sanskrit: ād id dha̱ nema̍ indri̱yaṁ ya̍janta̱ ād it pa̱ktiḥ pu̍ro̱ḻāśa̍ṁ riricyāt | ād it somo̱ vi pa̍pṛcyā̱d asu̍ṣvī̱n ād ij ju̍joṣa vṛṣa̱bhaṁ yaja̍dhyai ||
english: Then indeed they sacrifice the Indra-element; then the row of sacrificial cakes would outshine. Then the soma would thoroughly mix — even for those who have not pressed; then he has enjoyed to worship the bull.

sanskrit: kṛ̱ṇoty a̍smai̱ vari̍vo̱ ya i̱tthendrā̍ya̱ soma̍m uśa̱te su̱noti̍ | sa̱dhrī̱cīne̍na̱ mana̱sāvi̍vena̱n tam it sakhā̍yaṁ kṛṇute sa̱matsu̍ ||
english: He makes broad space for the one who thus, willingly, presses soma for Indra. With a unified, entering mind — him indeed he makes his companion in battles.

sanskrit: ya indrā̍ya su̱nava̱t soma̍m a̱dya pacā̍t pa̱ktīr u̱ta bhṛ̱jjāti̍ dhā̱nāḥ | prati̍ manā̱yor u̱cathā̍ni̱ harya̱n tasmi̍n dadha̱d vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ śuṣma̱m indra̍ḥ ||
english: He who today presses soma for Indra, cooks the ritual-cakes and roasts the grain — Indra, loving the lauds of both, places his virile force in that one.

sanskrit: ya̱dā sa̍ma̱ryaṁ vy ace̱d ṛghā̍vā dī̱rghaṁ yad ā̱jim a̱bhy akhya̍d a̱ryaḥ | aci̍krada̱d vṛṣa̍ṇa̱m patny acchā̍ duro̱ṇa ā niśi̍taṁ soma̱sudbhi̍ḥ ||
english: When the roaring one surveyed the arena of contest, when the lord looked out over the long race-course — the wife cried out toward the bull from the house, sharpened by the soma-pressers within.

sanskrit: bhūya̍sā va̱snam a̍cara̱t kanī̱yo 'vi̍krīto akāniṣa̱m puna̱r yan | sa bhūya̍sā̱ kanī̍yo̱ nāri̍recīd dī̱nā dakṣā̱ vi du̍hanti̱ pra vā̱ṇam ||
english: He went with a greater price — less; unsold I have desired coming back. He has not surpassed more with less — the feeble capacities milk out and drive forth the gain.

sanskrit: ka i̱maṁ da̱śabhi̱r mamendra̍ṁ krīṇāti dhe̱nubhi̍ḥ | ya̱dā vṛ̱trāṇi̱ jaṅgha̍na̱d athai̍nam me̱ puna̍r dadat ||
english: Who will buy this Indra of mine for ten milk-cows? When he has slain the Vṛtras, let them give him back to me again.

sanskrit: nū ṣṭu̱ta i̍ndra̱ nū gṛ̍ṇā̱na iṣa̍ṁ jari̱tre na̱dyo̱3̱̍ na pī̍peḥ | akā̍ri te harivo̱ brahma̱ navya̍ṁ dhi̱yā syā̍ma ra̱thya̍ḥ sadā̱sāḥ ||
english: Now praised, O Indra, now hymned, fill the lauder with refreshment as rivers fill — a fresh prayer has been made for you, O lord of tawny steeds; may we through vision be victorious charioteers, ever winning.

sanskrit: ko a̱dya naryo̍ de̱vakā̍ma u̱śann indra̍sya sa̱khyaṁ ju̍joṣa | ko vā̍ ma̱he 'va̍se̱ pāryā̍ya̱ sami̍ddhe a̱gnau su̱taso̍ma īṭṭe ||
english: Which virile man, god-desiring, willing today, has enjoyed Indra's friendship? Or who, with soma pressed and the fire kindled, entreats him for great crossing-aid?

sanskrit: ko nā̍nāma̱ vaca̍sā so̱myāya̍ manā̱yur vā̍ bhavati̱ vasta̍ u̱srāḥ | ka indra̍sya̱ yujya̱ṁ kaḥ sa̍khi̱tvaṁ ko bhrā̱traṁ va̍ṣṭi ka̱vaye̱ ka ū̱tī ||
english: Who has bent with speech for the soma-offering? Who is mindful of life, who passes the dawns? Who desires to be Indra's yoke-fellow? Who his friendship, who his brotherhood with the wise one? Who desires his aid?

sanskrit: ko de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīte̱ ka ā̍di̱tyām̐ adi̍ti̱ṁ jyoti̍r īṭṭe | kasyā̱śvinā̱v indro̍ a̱gniḥ su̱tasyā̱ṁśoḥ pi̍banti̱ mana̱sāvi̍venam ||
english: Who today chooses the aid of the gods? Who entreats the Ādityas, Aditi, the light? For whose pressed soma-stalk do the Aśvins, Indra, and Agni drink — entering with their mind?

sanskrit: tasmā̍ a̱gnir bhāra̍ta̱ḥ śarma̍ yaṁsa̱j jyok pa̍śyā̱t sūrya̍m u̱ccara̍ntam | ya indrā̍ya su̱navā̱mety āha̱ nare̱ naryā̍ya̱ nṛta̍māya nṛ̱ṇām ||
english: For him may the Bharata fire grant shelter — may he long see the sun rising. He who says 'Let us press soma for Indra' — to the manly one, the most manly of men.

sanskrit: na taṁ ji̍nanti ba̱havo̱ na da̱bhrā u̱rv a̍smā̱ adi̍ti̱ḥ śarma̍ yaṁsat | pri̱yaḥ su̱kṛt pri̱ya indre̍ manā̱yuḥ pri̱yaḥ su̍prā̱vīḥ pri̱yo a̍sya so̱mī ||
english: Neither many nor few conquer him; for him Aditi grants broad shelter. Dear to Indra is the one of good deeds, dear the mindful one; dear the one who provides well, dear to him the soma-drinker.

sanskrit: su̱prā̱vya̍ḥ prāśu̱ṣāḻ e̱ṣa vī̱raḥ suṣve̍ḥ pa̱ktiṁ kṛ̍ṇute̱ keva̱lendra̍ḥ | nāsu̍ṣver ā̱pir na sakhā̱ na jā̱mir du̍ṣprā̱vyo̍ 'vaha̱nted avā̍caḥ ||
english: This hero is well-helped, eats well; Indra alone makes the cooking of the good presser. For the non-presser there is no ally, no companion, no kinsman — hard to help, he drives away downward, speechlessly.

sanskrit: na re̱vatā̍ pa̱ṇinā̍ sa̱khyam indro 'su̍nvatā suta̱pāḥ saṁ gṛ̍ṇīte | āsya̱ veda̍ḥ khi̱dati̱ hanti̍ na̱gnaṁ vi suṣva̍ye pa̱ktaye̱ keva̍lo bhūt ||
english: The drinker of the pressed soma, Indra, does not agree to friendship with the wealthy miser who does not press. His knowledge grinds, smites the naked one; Indra alone belongs to the good presser, the good cooker.

sanskrit: indra̱m pare 'va̍re madhya̱māsa̱ indra̱ṁ yānto 'va̍sitāsa̱ indra̍m | indra̍ṁ kṣi̱yanta̍ u̱ta yudhya̍mānā̱ indra̱ṁ naro̍ vāja̱yanto̍ havante ||
english: The far ones, the near ones, and those in the middle call upon Indra; those going and those resting call upon Indra. Those dwelling and those fighting call upon Indra; men striving for prizes call upon Indra.
